newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end weak, underperform in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end weak, underperform in thin trade.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed weaker on Friday, with spreads to U.S. bonds widening, as minor profit-taking exaggerated price moves in an illiquid market, dealers said.
"There's been a lot of volatility. Liquidity is thin," said one Toronto-based trader. "Canada is just seeing a little bit of profit-taking. It's been outperforming for several weeks."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$1.15 to C$109.70 to yield 7.177 percent. The U.S. 30-year benchmark rose 15/32 to yield 6.81 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds widened to 37 basis points from 31 basis points at Thursday's close.

Traders said normally thin Friday trading was aggravated today by anti-government protests which shut down the public transit service in Toronto. Analysts said many in the financial community simply took the day off in order to avoid traffic disruptions which in the end failed to materialize.
"Clearly the day of protest had a small impact on liquidity, but not a major one," the trader said.
Otherwise, Canadian bonds opens sharply weaker on stronger-than-expected U.S. economic data.

North American fixed-income markets weakened sharply this morning after the U.S. Commerce Department reported that durable goods orders for September rose by 4.6 percent, well above expectations of a 2.0 percent rise.
However, U.S. Treasuries rebounded to strengthen later in the afternoon, while Canadian bonds remained weaker.

Dealers said investors have been taking profits on Canadian long bonds in the wake of their sharp outperformance against U.S. bonds earlier this week and for much of this month. Spreads fell to their lowest levels since 1985 on Tuesday.
In other prices, the Government of Canada 7.0 percent of 2006 fell C$0.95 to C$103.15 to yield 6.567 percent. The U.S. 10-year benchmark rose 8/32 to yield 6.54 percent.
The yield on the 10-year jumped to three basis points above the U.S. yield from a negative spread of two basis points at the close of trading on Thursday.
The three-month cash bill traded at 3.21 percent against the U.S. three-month bill at 5.12 percent.
